svg.text: Per-board USB power switching — 8-channel 12 V relay module wired to the HIL rig
Channel n switches ONLY the 5 V core of board n's USB cable. Boards run through NC: relay de-energised = board powered. Trigger jumpers on HIGH. DC− is common with Pi GND.
Powered USB hub (existing) — 5 V ≥4 A external PSU, uplink to Pi 5 USB 3.0
8-ch relay module, 12 V coils, opto-isolated inputs, high/low trigger jumpers (as received)
trigger select S1–S4: shunt on Com–High
trigger select S5–S8: shunt on Com–High
12 V + (relay coils only — never from the Pi)
Raspberry Pi 5 (runner host) — 40-pin header, board seen from above,
pin 1 at the microSD end; outer row = even pins. Own 27 W USB-C PSU.
Access: /dev/gpiochip* (label pinctrl-rp1), group gpio. GPIOs 12/16/18/20/21/23/24/25 are pull-down at boot.
Pi GND joins DC− here (signal return)
5 V USB VBUS, switched through NC/COM (2 short wires per board)
USB cable: D+, D−, GND untouched (breakout pass-through)
Relay input IN1–IN8 ← Pi GPIO (3.3 V high = relay ON = board OFF)
Pi GND → DC− (must be wired; USB shield is not the return)
Channel map (channel = hub port = board = udev name):
Drive test: pinctrl set 18 op dl (board 01 on) · pinctrl set 18 dh (board 01 cut) · pinctrl get 18
Never fit the Low jumper: with 12 V on DC+ a 3.3 V GPIO cannot pull IN high enough to switch the relay OFF.
